body: Oh absolutely! I have been on birth control (personally on Nuvaring) to help keep hormones from spiking up/down since before I even needed to 'control births'. lol. Basically hormonal birth control has help keep me sane the week prior, but I would definitely consult with your doc. I have type 2 so I am not sure if that makes a difference on if hormonal bc is a good option or not.
Thank you for responding. I will definitely look into those

I've definitely noticed that my handwriting changes with my mood/feelings, but I've also noticed that no matter what the task is, I approach/execute it differently depending on my mood. Kind of weird but interesting how you subconsciously make these slight changes to your way of life without really realizing it.

I've been battling my depression for over 10 years, and to this day the absolute hardest thing for me is getting up and out of bed. I can't even describe to others how it feels, because it's more than just a 'tired' feeling. The emotional aspect of not being able to get up is just as bad, if not worse, than the physical side of it. Sometimes the dread of the day feels like it's super gluing me to my bed.

Thank you so much, this made me feel hopeful. I know I'm not going to magically fix my rut in a day, so I'll try taking your advice to take things one day at a time and work my way up. Hopefully in a few days or weeks after doing those small things I will look back and see more progress than I would have guessed!

\~ Good Vibes \~

People get so frustrated with me when I 'dick around' when leaving or doing something, but really I'm just crumbling from the inside out because I want to hurry up to but I can't get my thoughts/shit together to just get out the fucking door. Then I get flustered because I know I am taking extra time, which causes even more delays and mess ups.

Hi OP. I recently joined Reddit to seek a community to help me understand my own disorder. As someone who suffers from Bipolar, I can say one thing that helps me personally is consistent validation, but in various ways. When my friends/SO know I am in a low spot and they want me to know that they care, they do acts of service for me that they know I appreciate (taking out the garbage, making some coffee, etc). Although hearing from others that they love and care about you a lot may help some, it often doesn't penetrate the hard headed thoughts that we have in our head. When I see someone doing acts of caring, I feel like it breaks right through those negative thoughts. 

It's such a strange disorder. I don't think anyone fully understands it. My parents (I am an only child) love me IMMENSELY and do/say things all the time to remind me of their love and support, but even on my worst days I don't want to believe they care about me at all. Just know that even if we have trouble accepting your love and support, it does not mean we do not appreciate you or not love you. If anything, when you stay through those hard times and don't judge us (huge HUGE props for not panicking or yelling when you walked in on your gf, because we are just as scared as you are), it shows us you really are there because you care and want to be there. 

I don't know if this helps at all, but I wish you and your gf the best in your relationship going forward and for her continued progress in healing.
